facts.fact: The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Cooperatives describes the Uganda National Bureau of Standards (UNBS) as the national standards body, overseen by a 10th National Standards Council, and says the Council reported 551 new standards developed in FY2025/26 (none identified as information technology or data).

note: No certification fact: the UNBS certification stated (enterprises certified rose from 501 to 1,270; Quality Mark) is product certification and the document names no information technology or data standard.

facts.fact: A notice approved 16 December 2025 by the Chair and Secretary of the National Standards Council cites the Uganda National Bureau of Standards Act, 1983 (Cap. 210) as the law under which the Council proposes 15 standards for compulsory declaration; all 15 are on cosmetics, paints, toys, chemicals, paper, appliances and cables, none on information technology or data.

note: No published or certification fact: none of the 15 listed Uganda Standards concerns information technology, security, software or data.

note: PPDA certified to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 (reported 2026-06-13, first of ten UDAP agencies) but the document names no certifier, so it is not recorded as a certification fact; it also names no national standard.

facts.fact: The report says the Uganda National Bureau of Standards is a statutory body under the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Cooperatives, established by the UNBS Act Cap 210, operational since 1989, governed by a National Standards Council that declares national standards, and holding 4,862 national standards at the end of FY2024/25 (Services and Management 773, none named as IT or data); the document dates the stated position to FY2024/25 (ended June 2025).
